newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Low margins push Elf into UK linkup.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Low margins push Elf into UK linkup.

text.p: French oil giant Elf said on Wednesday it was merging its British refining and retail operations with units of two U.S. oil companies in a $5 billion deal aimed at easing intense pressure on downstream margins.

Elf said it hoped to finalise the deal with Chevron Corp subsidiary Gulf Oil and Murco Petroleum, a unit Murphy Oil Corp early next year in a link-up which would shut Gulf's 115,000 barrels per day (bpd) British refinery in Pembroke, south Wales.
"The difficulties currently faced by the oil refining and marketing industry are well known," said Elf Oil U.K.'s managing director Christian Cleret.
"We recognise today that, for all three of us, this merger is the best option for a promising future as a new force to be reckoned with in the U.K. market."

Oversupply of refined products, the growing cost of meeting tough environmental regulations and fierce competition in the retail petrol market from oil majors like Exxon and supermarket chains had forced Elf's hand, industry analysts said.
"Companies are just not prepared to throw good money after bad in refining investment," said Salomon Brothers energy analyst Jeremy Hudson.
Analysts said the merger, which follows a similar Europe-wide link-up between British Petroleum and Mobil in February, was unlikely to be the last given the sector's bleak outlook.
"There are quite a few smaller players who must be feeling uncomfortable in the current market," said Morgan Stanley energy analyst Chris Buckley.
"The fact that Elf have acted in this way and that Chevron are a party to this shows how bad conditions have got," Salomon's Hudson said.

The merger, which will create a retail network of about 1,500 service stations with an estimated eight percent share of the British fuels market, would help reduce refining overcapacity and cut the companies' cost by about 50 million sterling per year.

Elf expects the move will cost 400-500 jobs -- about a third of the partners' total workforce -- mainly in south Wales, as the new joint venture concentrates refining at the existing Elf/Murphy refinery in Milford Haven from the middle of 1997.
"This merger involves taking difficult decisions today so that the new company and its employees will reap success tomorrow," said Gulf Oil's managing director David Setchell.

The new company, in which Elf and Gulf will each hold 41.25 percent and Murco 17.5 percent, will market all three brand names for both fuel and lubricants in the short-term but could unify under a single brand "in due course", Elf said.
Analysts said a cut in refining capacity in south Wales had been expected given the proximity of Texaco's 180,000 bpd plant at Pembroke and poor returns on exports.
"There was heavy reliance on gasoline exports to the U.S. The new joint venture will absorb more product than the refinery can produce so those should be a thing of the past," said Hudson.
Extra refined products for the retail network are expected to be obtained from Elf's system in France and the neighbouring Texaco refinery, industry source said.
Future downstream restructuring in Europe would not be confined to the minnows, analysts said.
Anglo-Dutch giant Royal Dutch/Shell is expected to complete a review of European refining operations by the end of the year. In May, Shell confirmed it was discussing options with other companies.
